archetype: An aristocrats sacrifice engine that kills by drain; strategic_frame.json declares 'combo' and the artifacts agree — five tutors, six declared kill lines, fourteen checker-passed stacks. The 30 creatures read as an aggro count only because in this deck the fodder IS the combo. COUNTING CONVENTION, held on every axis below: every figure is deck-audit's, taken over all 100 copies. Where the audit files a card's function under possible_uncounted (card-advantage, protection) the number is carried unchanged and the reading says what the oracle text shows.
verdict: The staples pass bought exactly what it claimed: RENEWABLE FODDER is now nine members drawn in 82.3% of games (72.2% by turn 6), the drain layer matches it at 82.3%, mean bodies at turn 6 is 4.239 in the committed artifact, and every mana axis is at target with the turn-3 land drop landing 91.6%. What binds is unchanged in name and narrower in content: interaction-breadth at 2 of 5 classes — zero artifact answers by enumeration of all 80 entries' oracle text — while three of the six declared kills are commander-gated and the recursion kills sit directly under the format's artifact-based graveyard hate. Behind it, fast mana (3 cards, 43.6%) is the smallest and lowest-rated multi-card engine class. The prescription is the prior diagnosis's two unapplied adds, re-validated against the new 99 with new natural cuts: Gate to Phyrexia and Culling the Weak.

single_points_of_failure.why: Three of the six declared kills (D, E, F) are commander-gated, including the primary. The gate is a timing tax, not an access problem — he recasts from the zone — but KILL E's 38.9% by-turn-6 assisted rate assumes he survives a rotation, and the cards that can hold him on the battlefield through a removal spell number three: Lightning Greaves plus the two instants the taxonomy cannot see (Supernatural Stamina, Malakir Rebirth). Recovering him afterwards from the graveyard (Victimize, Animate Dead, Phyrexian Reclamation) exists but costs the turn the gate is taxing. Mikaeus remains the only undying-GRANTER in the 99 (only Butcher Ghoul and Geralf's Messenger carry undying natively), but KILL F (stack 014, checker-passed, library-bounded — lethal to the pod in ~30 activations of the ~55 available) gives the undying loop a route that does not need him, which lowers the single-point weight the prior diagnosis put on Mikaeus alone.

cut_candidates.why: Four mana that does nothing the turn it lands, appears in zero checker-passed scenarios and zero declared kill lines, and overlaps a 12-copy interaction suite that is 50% over its floor. The staples pass held Deathgreeter explicitly so Grave Pact could keep its slot — the pilot has voted once, and this entry respects that by staying ranked, not mandated. It is still the weakest four-drop by artifact evidence.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: The deck's only repeatable non-targeting removal engine (sole removal:edict role in the 99); against hexproof or ward boards the remaining non-targeting answers are the three sweepers. With nine renewable fodder sources it triggers often, which is precisely why it is painful and not easy.

citations.quote: Walser's baseline is "at least 8-10 removal spells" inside a "15- to 20-card interactive suite"

cut_candidates.why: Recursion is five deep by enumeration (Agadeem's Awakening, Persist, Phyrexian Reclamation, Reassembling Skeleton, Victimize) and Victimize appears in zero checker-passed scenarios. Its job on the combo turn — return bodies to the battlefield — is covered for nonlegends by Persist at one mana less, for legends (Mikaeus) by Animate Dead, and at scale by Agadeem's Awakening; Persist alone does not cover it, because Persist reads 'nonlegendary'.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: The only recursion that returns TWO creatures for one card, and one of three ways in the 99 to put a legendary creature card (Mikaeus, KILL D's piece) from graveyard to battlefield — Animate Dead and Agadeem's Awakening at X>=6 are the others, since Persist is nonlegendary-only. Cutting it leaves two legend routes, one of them seven-plus mana. Its sacrifice cost is itself a death trigger for the drain layer. Recursion class goes 5 to 4.

open_questions.question: RESOLVED by stack 014 (checker pass at iteration 1, 22 citations): does KILL F function as declared? Yes, with one correction — 'unbounded' is REFUTED. Yawgmoth's draw is mandatory ('and draw a card', no 'may'), so every activation consumes a library card: ~55 activations available mid-game, lethal to the pod in ~30 (per two-activation cycle each opponent loses 2 to the drain and the Messenger-targeted seat 4, at net-zero life to the pilot), leaving ~25 cards of margin. goldfish_targets' KILL F label now carries the corrected wording: 'stack 014, library-bounded, lethal in ~30 activations'.
open_questions.why_it_matters: All six declared kills are now grounded in checker-passed artifacts. KILL F is fact, but a library-bounded fact — it kills the pod with margin and must never be presented as an unbounded loop. The reduction of Mikaeus's single-point weight that leaned on this line now stands on a verified stack.

open_questions.question: Under Grafdigger's Cage, do KILL A (009), KILL B (011), KILL D (010) and now KILL F still function? A and B cast Gravecrawler from the graveyard, D and F return creature cards from the graveyard via undying — all four look Cage-shaped, which is the concrete case for Gate to Phyrexia.
open_questions.why_it_matters: If all four die to one two-mana artifact the deck cannot answer, the Gate add is undersold here, not oversold.

open_questions.question: Under an opposing Cursed Totem, what survives of the outlet component? Five of its eight members are creatures with activated abilities, and Yawgmoth himself is shut off.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether the artifact-answer gap is merely about graveyard hate or also about the outlet class.

open_questions.question: How often does the deck assemble ANY of its six kills? The audit's schema states it cannot express the union, and averaging would invent a number the simulation never measured.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The per-line rates (0.6%-13.5% unassisted) understate the deck's real conversion; the union is the number a pilot actually experiences.

open_questions.question: Should the fast-mana any_of be re-curated after the purchase lands — adding Culling the Weak if bought, and deciding whether Jet Medallion belongs (it accelerates Yawgmoth to an effective 3 but is cost-reduction, not mana)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 43.6% figure is only as good as the declared group; a stale declaration would leave the next diagnosis prescribing against a number the deck has already moved.
